prompt: Compare PLA, ABS, and PETG filaments used in FDM 3D printing. Specifically, contrast their temperature requirements and bed adhesion characteristics.
rawOutput:
# PLA vs. ABS vs. PETG: Temperature & Bed Adhesion Comparison

## Temperature Requirements

| Property | PLA | ABS | PETG |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Extrusion Temperature** | 180–220 °C | 220–250 °C | 230–260 °C |
| **Bed Temperature** | 50–70 °C (often none needed) | 80–110 °C | 60–80 °C |
| **Cooling Fan** | High (benefits from rapid cooling) | Low to moderate (warp-prone) | Moderate (balanced) |
| **Glass Transition Temp (Tg)** | ~60 °C | ~105 °C | ~80 °C |

### Key Differences

- **PLA** prints at the lowest temperatures and is the most forgiving for beginners. It cools quickly, which actually helps layer adhesion.
- **ABS** requires significantly higher nozzle and bed temperatures. It is prone to warping if the bed is too cool or if parts cool too quickly during printing.
- **PETG** sits in the middle temperature-wise but is unique in that it requires a relatively hot nozzle while still performing well on a moderately heated bed. It is less sensitive to cooling rates than ABS.

---

## Bed Adhesion Characteristics

| Property | PLA | ABS | PETG |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Adhesion to Glass** | Excellent (especially with slight cooling) | Good (with glue stick or PEI) | Good to excellent |
| **Adhesion to Build Plate** | Very strong (can be difficult to remove) | Strong but prone to warping | Strong, easy to remove |
| **Warping Tendency** | Very low | High (requires enclosure for best results) | Low to moderate |
| **Release Agent Needed** | Rarely | Often (glue stick, hairspray, ABS juice) | Rarely |
| **Enclosure Benefit** | Minimal | Significant (reduces warping) | Moderate |

### Key Differences

- **PLA** adheres almost too aggressively to glass beds. Some printers deliberately run the bed slightly cool or use a thin layer of glue to make removal easier. It rarely needs an enclosure.
- **ABS** is notorious for warping. The corners of large prints peel off the bed as they cool and contract. Solutions include a heated enclosure, brim or raft structures, ABS juice (dissolved ABS in acetone), and high bed temperatures. Without an enclosure, warping is common even with proper bed adhesion.
- **PETG** offers a good compromise. It bonds well to glass and PEI sheets, releases cleanly, and is far less prone to warping than ABS. It benefits from an enclosure in cold environments but can print well without one.

---

## Summary

| Aspect | PLA | ABS | PETG |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ease of Printing** | ★★★★★ | ★★☆☆☆ | ★★★★☆ |
| **Temperature Sensitivity** | Low | High | Moderate |
| **Warping Risk** | Minimal | High | Low |
| **Bed Adhesion Reliability** | Excellent | Moderate (with effort) | Excellent |
| **Best For** | Prototyping, hobby, food-safe parts | Functional parts, mechanical strength | Functional parts, food-safe, strong bonds |

**PLA** is the easiest all-around filament but is brittle and heat-sensitive. **ABS** offers superior mechanical strength and heat resistance but demands more from the printer and user. **PETG** combines ease of use with strong mechanical properties and reliable bed adhesion, making it the most versatile of the three for many applications.
